sci-repo-y7-aran-undated-bioend-mc-1.title: Year 7 Science — Biology end-of-topic test — Aranmore, undated (original source MC)
sci-repo-y7-aran-undated-bioend-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: Some plants are known as weeds. Describe a weed.
options: A plant that does not grow very well
A plant that grows where it is not wanted
A plant that grows out of control
A plant that does not produce flowers
questions.explanation: A weed is a plant growing where unwanted.

questions.prompt: Identify the characteristic that would be suitable for use in a strong key to identify dogs.
options: The presence of a patch of different coloured fur around their eye
Whether they were short-haired or long-haired
questions.explanation: Presence/absence of a distinct patch is the clearest binary observable choice among these options; continuous traits need explicit cut-offs.

questions.prompt: Identify which of the following statements about the levels of classification is true.
options: There are more different types of organisms in a class compared to a genus.
Phylum is a group within a family.
There are many classes within an order.
The organisms within a kingdom are most like each other.
questions.explanation: A class is a broader rank than a genus in the stated hierarchy.

questions.prompt: Select the best description of the term binomial nomenclature.
options: A system or scientific naming that was used in the past but is no longer used.
Using only two names to identify any living thing.
A system of naming that does not change.
A shorthand version of the name of an organism.
questions.explanation: B is intended: a two-part scientific name for a species, genus plus specific epithet. “Any living thing” is imprecise; informal two-word names are not necessarily binomials.

questions.prompt: Select the plants from this group that are most closely related: Hakea sericea  Grevillea sericea Hakea pachyphylla Acacia pachyphylla
questions.explanation: The two Hakea species share the same genus.

questions.prompt: Read the four statements below, then deduce which pair of organisms are most alike. A and B belong to the same Genus. A and C belong to the same Order. C and B belong to the same Family. They all belong to the same Kingdom as D.
questions.explanation: A and B share genus, the most specific shared rank stated.

questions.prompt: Identify the phylum this animal belongs to. It lives in water. It filters its food out of the water that passes through the pores in its body. Wastes and water are pushed out through a hole in the top of its body.
Identify the phylum this animal belongs to. It lives in water or very moist places. It is bilaterally symmetrical with a body flattened from top to bottom. Many are scavengers in the ocean.
questions.explanation: Platyhelminthes/flatworms match the flattened bilateral body description.

questions.prompt: 10 Identify the class this fish belongs to. It has a skeleton made of cartilage and a fully functioning jaw
questions.explanation: Chondrichthyes/cartilaginous fishes; source misspells the class name.

questions.prompt: An animal with an exoskeleton must moult before it can grow. This means that the animal gets rid of its old, small exoskeleton and forms a new and larger one. Moulting happens when the casing or shell cracks open and drops off. A new, larger exoskeleton then forms. It starts soft but then hardens to form a new shell or casing for the animal. Empty and dried shell-like casings of cicadas are often found on trees. Identify which of the following best describes these casings:
options: The casings are the old exoskeletons of cicadas that were moulted when the cicadas  grew.
The cicadas are growing within these casings but are currently too small to see.
The casings are the eggs of new cicadas.
The casings are the remains of dead cicadas.
questions.explanation: The casings are shed old exoskeletons, A. A replacement cuticle develops beneath the old one and expands/hardens after moulting; the simplified source sequence should not be read as no cuticle existing immediately after shedding.

questions.prompt: Chordates have a skeleton inside their bodies. This type of skeleton is known as an endoskeleton. An exoskeleton is very different. An exoskeleton is a hard, external skeleton that forms a shell or casing around the animal, its body, head, tail and legs. Arthropods have an exoskeleton. Identify which of the following is the best meaning for the prefixes endo and exo when discussing skeletons:
options: endo and exo both mean the same thing.
endo means external, exo means internal.
endo means internal, exo means external.
endo means that an animal has a skeleton, exo means that an animal has none.
questions.explanation: C: endo means internal and exo external. The source’s broad claim that all chordates have an internal skeleton is oversimplified; the prefix distinction remains clear.
